entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.0075 of 2023, under Sections 323, 504, 506,
376D IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Jayas, District Amethi.

3. The FIR in question was lodged initially alleging that one Amarnath, named in the FIR used to tease the daughter of the informant and used to mis-handle her, committing the offence under Section 354 IPC.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the statement was made against the applicant as well as Amarnath was name in the FIR with regard to offence committed Arjeet Kumar vs State Of U.P. 1 under Section 354 IPC.

entities.text: Arjeet Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home And 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No allegations with regard to commission of rape was made on the said date.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the allegation with regard to commission of rape was made against the applicant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that at the time of lodging of FIR, the informant was accompanied by his daughter, the victim as well as her husband and, thus, there was no reason to not to allege the commission of the offence under Section 376 IPC.
He further draws my attention to the medical on record, which demonstrates that the date of L.M.P. (last monthly period) was 03.03.2023.
The incident is said to have occurred on 6.3.2023 which makes the scene improbable.
He further argues that even in the medical report, no injuries were recorded and the victim was found to be menstruating on the said date of medical examination which was done on 6.3.2023.

In the light of the said, he argues that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the said case and should be enlarged on bail and he is languishing in jail since 1.4.2023 and has no previous criminal antecedent.

5. Learned AGA strongly opposes the bail application by arguing that the name of the applicant was subsequently stated under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and, thus, no case for bail is made out as the victim is around 14 years of age.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar, there are huge variance in the statements recorded in the FIR or the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the medical report prima facie belies the averments made in the statements, there is no reason to believe as to why the name of the applicant was not mentioned in the FIR or in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

Considering the said fact couple with the fact that the applicant has no previous criminal antecedent and is languishing in jail since1.4.2023, as such the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

7. Let the applicantArjeet Kumar be released on bail in Case Crime No.0075 of 2023, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 376D IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station-Jayas, District Amethi subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
